phrases.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish,
phrases.text: The hands stand for what he did, and the words mean his deeds are lost and perished. Tabari says the surah came down after the Prophet called his kinsfolk on the hill of al-Safa, and Abu Lahab mocked him for gathering them.
This is a statement of fact, not a wish, which is why the reading of Abdullah has the word already. Tabari compares it to saying of someone: may God destroy you, and: he has indeed destroyed you.
What did his wealth avail him, and did it turn the wrath of God away from him?

And what he earned, which means his children. Tabari gives the story: the sons of Abu Lahab came to Ibn Abbas disputing over the house, and he was pushed onto the bed, and he said: take these evil earnings away from me.

phrases.translation: He will burn in a flaming Fire
phrases.text: Abu Lahab will soon burn in a fire that blazes.
His wife will burn in it with him.

The commentators differed. Some said she carried thorns and threw them on the path of the Prophet to pierce his foot as he went out to pray. Others said she spread tales and mocked him for his poverty. Tabari takes the thorns to be the plainest sense, and adds the story of her asking him why he mocked her.
